acceptance:
  - claim: >-
      `finish.write_findings` takes an optional keyword `heads`, a mapping
      from task key to a graded head, empty by default, and hands it to
      `_layer_findings`. There, a `qualifications` row whose `lens` is not
      one of `review.LENSES` carries `heads`'s own entry for that row's
      layer as its `head`, in place of the layer's `pushed_sha`. A row
      whose `lens` is one of `review.LENSES`, and every entry
      `_left_by_critic` adds, still carry `pushed_sha` regardless of
      `heads`. A layer `heads` does not name keeps `pushed_sha` on every
      one of its own rows, in-cell and critic entries included. The
      witness drives a two-layer stack: one layer is a generation-1 layer
      named in `heads` at a head apart from its `pushed_sha`, with one
      end-review row, one join row, one in-cell row and one critic
      finding; the other is a generation-0 layer with one end-review row,
      left out of `heads`.
    witness: tests/test_cli.py::test_write_findings_takes_heads_and_labels_only_end_review_and_join_rows_with_it
    mutant:
      file: saffron/finish.py
      find: 'head = packaged_head if row["lens"] in review.LENSES else graded_head'
      replace: 'head = graded_head if row["lens"] in review.LENSES else packaged_head'
    wrong_versions:
      - "`heads` is ignored, so every row still carries `packaged_head`."
      - Every row of a named layer takes the graded head, in-cell rows included.
      - A critic entry takes the graded head in place of `packaged_head`.
      - A layer missing from `heads` gets `None` as its head, rather than its `pushed_sha`.
      - "`heads` is looked up by `spec_id`, so a mapping keyed by task key is never matched."
      - Only the `spec` lens takes the graded head, so a `join` row keeps `packaged_head`.
      - "`write_findings` never passes `heads` on to `_layer_findings`."
      - "`heads` defaults to a dict literal, shared across every call rather than fresh each time."
  - claim: >-
      Without `heads`, `write_findings` still labels every row of every
      layer with that layer's own `pushed_sha`, critic entries and
      in-cell rows included.
    witness: tests/test_finish.py::test_findings_json_holds_each_layers_findings_and_each_follow_up_that_added_no_layer
    preserves: true
---

## Context

Backlog item **b-8a0c9a**, under `DESIGN.md` §5.7 and ADR 7. This follow-up
grows out of a finding on `SA-0303`'s own end review, filed against
`saffron/finish.py:259` at that spec's head
`4f53899cb922aa5d666a70550248067757746fb8`. `SA-0303`'s Out-of-scope
section already names the gap: `_layer_findings` labels every
qualification row with `head = layer["pushed_sha"]`
(`saffron/finish.py:259`), the packaged head, even though `SA-0303` can now
anchor and line-number a row against the end review's *graded* range
instead (`qualify.py`'s `graded_fields` path, `saffron/qualify.py:193-203`).
`write_findings` runs at the end of every normal stack batch
(`saffron/cli.py:1033`), so `findings.json` can report a `file`/`line` that
only exists at the graded head under a `head` naming the packaged one, a
mismatch whenever a branch moved between PACKAGE and the end review.
`SA-0303` defers the fix to `SA-0306`.

Every line below was read at `4f53899cb922aa5d666a70550248067757746fb8`.

**Why this spec touches only `saffron/finish.py` and `tests/test_cli.py`.**
A follow-up candidate's `touches` must stay inside the set `write_follow_ups`
hands its prompt: the finding's own file plus every test path the stack's
diff changed (`saffron/follow_up.py:319`, checked at `:210-212`). That set
holds no path in `saffron/cli.py`, so the wiring that would fill a real
`heads` mapping from a batch's own end review, and hand it to
`write_findings` at its one call site (`saffron/cli.py:1033`), stays out of
reach here. This spec adds the capability `_layer_findings` reads; a later
spec wires a real caller to it, the way `SA-0306`'s own draft already plans
to (`.saffron/specs/SA-0306-*.md`, Problem 3).

**`_layer_findings` today.** It reads `layer["task_key"]` and
`layer["spec_id"]`, then sets `head = layer["pushed_sha"]`
(`saffron/finish.py:253-259`). It walks `ledger.qualifications`, remapping
`qualified` through `pooled`, and appends one dict per kept row, every one
carrying that same `head` (`:261-282`). A generation-1 layer's own critic
findings are appended through `_left_by_critic`, passed that same `head`
too (`:283-284`). `ledger.stack_layers` is where `task_key` comes from, one
column of the row this function reads (`saffron/ledger.py:1768-1783`).

**`write_findings` today.** It takes `pooled` as its only keyword, reads
`ledger.stack_layers(batch_id)`, and calls `_layer_findings` once per layer
with no other argument (`saffron/finish.py:288-307`). Its docstring says
nothing about a graded head (`:296-300`).

**The two lens sets a row's `head` must tell apart.** An in-cell REVIEW
concern's `lens` is one of `review.LENSES`
(`saffron/phases/review.py:41-46`): its line was recorded against the
layer's packaged head, never a graded one, because `SA-0303` qualifies an
in-cell concern over the packaged range on purpose. An end-review row's
`lens` is one of `END_LENSES` (`saffron/end_review.py:43-46`), or it is the
literal `"join"`; either way it can now be anchored and line-numbered
against a graded range. `_left_by_critic` only ever reads a lens in
`review.LENSES` (`saffron/finish.py:230-250`), so its own entries are
always in-cell ones.

**What a later spec would fill `heads` from.** `StackReview.fields` maps a
task key to the `LayerFields` the end review graded that layer at
(`saffron/end_review.py:672-680`). `qualify.graded_fields` already reads
that same mapping with the same packaged-head fallback
(`saffron/qualify.py:193-203`), the precedent this spec's `heads.get`
follows for `_layer_findings`.

## Problem

1. **`_layer_findings` takes `heads`.** A required positional `heads:
   Mapping[str, str]`, keyed by task key. It reads `layer["pushed_sha"]` as
   `packaged_head` and `heads.get(task_key, packaged_head)` as
   `graded_head`. Each row's `head` is `packaged_head` when the row's
   `lens` is one of `review.LENSES`, and `graded_head` otherwise. Every
   `_left_by_critic` entry keeps `packaged_head` explicitly, so a changed
   local never reaches it by accident.
2. **`write_findings` takes `heads` too.** An optional keyword `heads:
   Mapping[str, str] | None`, `None` by default. It resolves `heads or {}`
   once and hands that mapping to every `_layer_findings` call. Its own
   call to `ledger.batch_follow_ups` and the `_left_by_critic` calls that
   follow stay untouched: a follow-up that added no layer is never graded,
   so `heads` holds no entry for one, and nothing there needs to ask.
3. **Both docstrings say what `heads` does.** `_layer_findings`'s and
   `write_findings`'s, each naming the fallback and the `review.LENSES`
   exemption.

## Out of scope

- **Any real caller of `heads`.** No file in this spec's allowed paths can
  wire a batch's own end review into it. `saffron/cli.py`'s one call to
  `write_findings` (`:1033`) keeps passing no `heads`, so this change alone
  leaves every batch's `findings.json` exactly as it reads today.
- **`commit_finish` and `publish_finish`.** Both still build on and check
  against `layer["pushed_sha"]` alone. The finding this spec answers names
  only `_layer_findings`'s `head`, not the finishing commit's parent or the
  branch-moved escalation.
- **How the end review grades a layer, and `StackReview.fields`.**
  `SA-0302` owns both.
- **A follow-up that added no layer.** It never reaches `heads`, by design
  (Problem 2).

## Notes for the agent

**Which criterion is an edit.** Criterion 1 mutates a line the change
keeps: the `if row["lens"] in review.LENSES` choice between
`packaged_head` and `graded_head`. Leave `_left_by_critic`'s own
`packaged_head` argument untouched, so a mutant swapping the row-level
choice cannot also flip the critic path. Criterion 2 names a test that
exists now at base and changes nothing here; `preserves: true` and no
`mutant`.

**The fixture is a plain ledger, no git.** `write_findings` reads only the
ledger, so build two tasks with `create_run`, `create_task`,
`set_task_package` and `record_stack_layer`, one generation 0 at the
bottom and one generation 1 at the top. Give the top task's own key an
entry in `heads` at a third sha, apart from its `pushed_sha`. Record one
`qualifications` row per lens case with `ledger.record_qualification`
(lens `spec` on the bottom layer, lens `spec`, lens `join` and a lens in
`review.LENSES` on the top layer), and one critic finding on the top layer
through `ledger.record_findings`. Call `write_findings` with `heads={top_key:
top_graded}`, read the written `dest` back with `json.loads`, and assert
each row's `head` by its own `claim`.

**Measured on a prototype at `4f53899cb922aa5d666a70550248067757746fb8`.**
It passed both witnesses, the whole of `tests/test_cli.py` and
`tests/test_finish.py`, and the `lint`, `format`, `types` and `dead`
gates. The new witness failed with `saffron/finish.py` reverted to its
base text, and failed again under the declared mutant; both failures
restored to green once undone. Its diff measured 1108 changed tokens, 390
of them outside `tests/`.

**Docstrings at the cap.** New comments and docstrings take no em dash,
semicolon, contraction, perfect tense or sentence over 25 words, and the
`prose` gate caps a function docstring at 10 lines. Split a long sentence
into two shorter ones that are each still true, rather than joining them
with a semicolon.
